page: Microsoft Azure M128-64bds_3_v3 is a memory-optimized server belonging to the MBDSMediumMemoryv3 family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8473C processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, configured with 32 physical cores and 64 dedicated vCPUs running at a clock speed of 4.0 GHz. The hardware features 2794.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 43.66 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled with a capacity of 6144 GB, and the system is Premium Storage capable. The virtualization layer is managed by Microsoft Hyper-V.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core processing capabilities, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 67529.51 and a PassMark CPU score of 81742.61. Memory performance is a key highlight, with large-block read-only memory bandwidth reaching a top-tier 367.66 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 169.25 GB/sec. Database operations are highly efficient, as evidenced by a top-tier PassMark database score of 35100.58 and Redis SET operations performing at 87.35 million operations per second. The CPU supports Advanced Vector Extensions and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which assist in workloads like LLM inference, where prompt processing speeds reach 235.07 tokens/sec for a medium 7B model.

Given its massive memory footprint and bundled 6144 GB local storage, this server offers high resource density for memory-bound applications. The qualitative cost efficiency is centered on its ability to consolidate large-scale databases and in-memory workloads onto a single node without requiring distributed clustering. It is highly suited for large relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, data analytics, and memory-intensive enterprise applications.

It excels in database performance, demonstrating a top-tier PassMark database score of 35100.58 and 87.35 million Redis SET operations per second. Supported by Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), it also handles medium-scale LLM inference efficiently. This server is highly suited for large-scale in-memory databases, enterprise caching, and heavy analytical workloads requiring massive memory capacity and local storage.
